TEXT.English: Please support [OUR_CIV_SHORT] and its people. We depend on your help!
TEXT.French: Veuillez soutenir le [OUR_CIV_SHORT] et son peuple. Nous avons besoin de votre aide !
TEXT.German: Please support [OUR_CIV_SHORT] and it's people. We depend on your help!
TEXT.Italian: Please support [OUR_CIV_SHORT] and it's people. We depend on your help!
TEXT.Spanish: Please support [OUR_CIV_SHORT] and it's people. We depend on your help!

TEXT.English: This will be of mutual benefit for us both, don't you think so?
TEXT.French: Ceci nous bénéficiera mutuellement, ne croyez-vous pas ?
TEXT.German: This will be of mutual benefit for us both, don't you think so?
TEXT.Italian: This will be of mutual benefit for us both, don't you think so?
TEXT.Spanish: This will be of mutual benefit for us both, don't you think so?

TEXT.English: Our armies are evenly matched, but I believe in a battle I would win out. So that this does not occur I ask you to meet our demands.
TEXT.French: Nos armées sont de force égale, mais je crois que nous gagnerions en cas de guerre. Si vous voulez éviter cela, veuillez accéder à nos demandes.
TEXT.German: Unsere Armeen sind ebenbürtig, aber ich denke, ich würde einen Kampf gewinnen. Damit das nicht geschieht, solltet Ihr unseren Forderungen nachkommen.
TEXT.Italian: I nostri eserciti si equivalgono, ma sono sicuro che in una battaglia vincerei io. Affinché ciò non accada, ti chiedo di soddisfare le nostre richieste.
TEXT.Spanish: Nuestros ejércitos están a la par, aunque creo que yo ganaría si lucharan. Así que, para que esto no ocurra, os pido que satisfagáis mis exigencias.

TEXT.English: [OUR_CIV_SHORT] needs this and demands your assistance!
TEXT.French: [OUR_CIV_SHORT] a besoin de ceci et demande votre aide !
TEXT.German: [OUR_CIV_SHORT] needs this and demands your assistance!
TEXT.Italian: [OUR_CIV_SHORT] needs this and demands your assistance!
TEXT.Spanish: [OUR_CIV_SHORT] needs this and demands your assistance!

TEXT.English: Brazil is strong in many ways, [CT_NAME]. Do not force me to show you how strong.
TEXT.French: Le Brésil est fort, [CT_NAME]. Ne me poussez pas à vous montrer à quel point.
TEXT.German: Brazil is strong in many ways, [CT_NAME]. Do not force me to show you how strong.
TEXT.Italian: Brazil is strong in many ways, [CT_NAME]. Do not force me to show you how strong.
TEXT.Spanish: Brazil is strong in many ways, [CT_NAME]. Do not force me to show you how strong.

TEXT.English: You are outgunned and outclassed. I suggest you give me what I demand.
TEXT.French: Vous êtes inférieurs en nombre et en armes. Je vous suggère de me donner ce que je veux.
TEXT.German: Ihr seid uns in jeder Hinsicht unterlegen. Ich schlage vor, Ihr gebt mir, was ich verlange.
TEXT.Italian: Ti supero in classe ed equipaggiamento. Ti suggerisco di darmi quello che voglio.
TEXT.Spanish: Os superamos en armas y en hombres. Os sugiero que nos deis lo que exijo.

TEXT.English: Can you spare this for the people of the [OUR_EMPIRE]?
TEXT.French: Pourriez-vous fournir ceci au peuple du [OUR_EMPIRE] ?
TEXT.German: Can you spare this for the people of the [OUR_EMPIRE]?
TEXT.Italian: Can you spare this for the people of the [OUR_EMPIRE]?
TEXT.Spanish: Can you spare this for the people of the [OUR_EMPIRE]?

TEXT.English: My people have faith in me, [CT_NAME]. Please help me not to disappoint them.
TEXT.French: Mon peuple a foi en moi, [CT_NAME]. Aidez-moi à ne pas le décevoir.
TEXT.German: My people have faith in me, [CT_NAME]. Please help me not to disappoint them.
TEXT.Italian: My people have faith in me, [CT_NAME]. Please help me not to disappoint them.
TEXT.Spanish: My people have faith in me, [CT_NAME]. Please help me not to disappoint them.

TEXT.English: The simplest strategy is for me to ask you for what we need and hope your good will wins out.
TEXT.French: Le plus simple serait de vous demander de nous aider en espérant que votre bonne volonté fera le reste.
TEXT.German: Es ist für mich die einfachste Strategie, Euch um das zu bitten, was wir benötigen, und darauf zu hoffen, dass Euer guter Wille siegt.
TEXT.Italian: La strategia più semplice per me è chiederti quello che ci serve e sperare nella tua buona volontà.
TEXT.Spanish: La estrategia más sencilla para mí es pediros lo que necesitamos y rezar porque vuestra buena voluntad se imponga.

TEXT.English: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! I am [OUR_NAME], leader of the great civilization of [OUR_CIV_SHORT].
TEXT.French: Salutations, [CT_NAME]! Je suis [OUR_NAME], souverain de la grande civilisation de [OUR_CIV_SHORT].
TEXT.German: Seid gegrüßt, [CT_NAME]! Ich bin [OUR_NAME], Anführer der großen Zivilisation von [OUR_CIV_SHORT].
TEXT.Italian: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! I am [OUR_NAME], leader of the great civilization of [OUR_CIV_SHORT].
TEXT.Spanish: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! I am [OUR_NAME], leader of the great civilization of [OUR_CIV_SHORT].

TEXT.English: Hola. I am [OUR_NAME] of the [OUR_EMPIRE]. I am convinced that the good intentions of a ruler are simply not enough and that the collective factor represented by the workers is indispensable. Don't you agree [CT_NAME]?
TEXT.French: Hola. Je suis [OUR_NAME] du [OUR_EMPIRE]. Je suis convaincu que les bonnes intentions d'un souverain ne sont pas suffisantes et que le facteur collectif représenté par les travailleurs est indispensable. N'êtes-vous pas d'accord, [CT_NAME] ?
TEXT.German: Hola. I am [OUR_NAME] of the [OUR_EMPIRE]. I am convinced that the good intentions of a ruler are simply not enough and that the collective factor represented by the workers is indispensable. Don't you agree [CT_NAME]?
TEXT.Italian: Hola. I am [OUR_NAME] of the [OUR_EMPIRE]. I am convinced that the good intentions of a ruler are simply not enough and that the collective factor represented by the workers is indispensable. Don't you agree [CT_NAME]?
TEXT.Spanish: Hola. I am [OUR_NAME] of the [OUR_EMPIRE]. I am convinced that the good intentions of a ruler are simply not enough and that the collective factor represented by the workers is indispensable. Don't you agree [CT_NAME]?

TEXT.English: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. My name is [OUR_NAME], and I am the president of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. My motto is: when there is respect, there is peace!
TEXT.French: Salutations, [CT_NAME]. Je m'appelle [OUR_NAME], et je suis président du [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. Ma devise est la suivante : là où règne le respect règne la paix !
TEXT.German: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. My name is [OUR_NAME], and I am the president of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. My motto is: when there is respect, there is peace!
TEXT.Italian: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. My name is [OUR_NAME], and I am the president of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. My motto is: when there is respect, there is peace!
TEXT.Spanish: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. My name is [OUR_NAME], and I am the president of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. My motto is: when there is respect, there is peace!

TEXT.English: Greetings. I am [OUR_NAME], Emperor of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. Dedicating all my efforts to the well-being of my people, I shall guard the concept of Autocracy like all my forefathers did.
TEXT.French: Bonjour. Je suis [OUR_NAME], empereur de [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. Et dédiant tous mes efforts au bien-être de mon peuple, je défendrai l'idée de l'autocratie comme l'ont fait tous mes ancêtres.
TEXT.German: Grüße. Ich bin [OUR_NAME], Kaiser von [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. Während ich all meine Anstrengungen dem Wohlergehen meines Volkes widme, werde ich das Konzept der Autokratie beschützen wie alle meine Vorväter.
TEXT.Italian: Greetings. I am [OUR_NAME], Emperor of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. Dedicating all my efforts to the well-being of my people, I shall guard the concept of Autocracy like all my forefathers did.
TEXT.Spanish: Greetings. I am [OUR_NAME], Emperor of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. Dedicating all my efforts to the well-being of my people, I shall guard the concept of Autocracy like all my forefathers did.

TEXT.English: Welcome to humble [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. I am [OUR_NAME], leader of this far-reaching and ever progressing country. Tell me, who are you?
TEXT.French: Bienvenue dans l'humble [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. Je suis [OUR_NAME], souverain de ce grand pays en progrès constant. Dites-moi, qui êtes-vous ?
TEXT.German: Welcome to humble [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. I am [OUR_NAME], leader of this far-reaching and ever progressing country. Tell me, who are you?
TEXT.Italian: Welcome to humble [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. I am [OUR_NAME], leader of this far-reaching and ever progressing country. Tell me, who are you?
TEXT.Spanish: Welcome to humble [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. I am [OUR_NAME], leader of this far-reaching and ever progressing country. Tell me, who are you?

TEXT.English: Hello, friend. My name is [OUR_NAME], but you can call me Jose. Or you can call me Francisco. Or you can call me Martin. Just don't call me late for dinner.
TEXT.French: Bonjour, mon ami. Je m'appelle [OUR_NAME], mais vous pouvez m'appeler José. Ou Francisco. Ou Martin. Evitez simplement de m'appeler trop tard pour dîner.
TEXT.German: Hallo. Ich bin [OUR_NAME], aber Ihr könnt mich Jose nennen. Oder nennt mich Francisco. Oder nennt mich Martin. Hauptsache Ihr nennt meinen Namen im Zusammenhang mit einer Einladung zum Essen.
TEXT.Italian: Salve, amico. Il mio nome è [OUR_NAME], ma puoi chiamarmi Jose. O puoi chiamarmi Francisco. O puoi chiamarmi Martin. Basta che non mi chiami troppo tardi per la cena.
TEXT.Spanish: Hola, amigo. Soy [OUR_NAME], pero podéis llamarme José, o Francisco, o Martín. Pero no me llaméis tarde para la cena.

TEXT.English: Hello, [CT_NAME]. I am General Santa Anna, Savior of Mexico! What have you come to offer me in tribute?
TEXT.French: Bonjour, [CT_NAME]. Je suis le général Santa Anna, sauveur du Mexique ! Que venez-vous m'offrir en tribut ?
TEXT.German: Hello, [CT_NAME]. I am General Santa Anna, Savior of Mexico! What have you come to offer me in tribute?
TEXT.Italian: Hello, [CT_NAME]. I am General Santa Anna, Savior of Mexico! What have you come to offer me in tribute?
TEXT.Spanish: Hello, [CT_NAME]. I am General Santa Anna, Savior of Mexico! What have you come to offer me in tribute?

TEXT.English: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! It is so great to be at peace with you glorious nation!
TEXT.French: Salutations, [CT_NAME] ! Qu'il est bon d'être en paix avec votre glorieuse nation !
TEXT.German: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! It is so great to be at peace with you glorious nation!
TEXT.Italian: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! It is so great to be at peace with you glorious nation!
TEXT.Spanish: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! It is so great to be at peace with you glorious nation!

TEXT.English: I see you have come to visit, [CT_NAME]. Tell me what is it you wish to discuss.
TEXT.French: Je constate que vous êtes venu nous visiter, [CT_NAME]. Dites-moi de quoi vous voulez discuter.
TEXT.German: I see you have come to visit, [CT_NAME]. Tell me, what is it you wish to discuss.
TEXT.Italian: I see you have come to visit, [CT_NAME]. Tell me, what is it you wish to discuss.
TEXT.Spanish: I see you have come to visit, [CT_NAME]. Tell me, what is it you wish to discuss.

TEXT.English: Finally I get to talk to a worthy adversary. What can the [OUR_EMPIRE] do for you?
TEXT.French: Enfin un adversaire à ma mesure ! Que peut faire l'[OUR_EMPIRE] pour vous ?
TEXT.German: Endlich kann ich mich mit einem würdigen Gegner unterhalten. Was kann das [OUR_EMPIRE:2] für Euch tun?
TEXT.Italian: Finalmente parlo con un degno avversario. Cosa può fare [OUR_EMPIRE] per te?
TEXT.Spanish: Por fin consigo hablar con un adversario digno. ¿Qué puede hacer el [OUR_EMPIRE] por vos?

TEXT.English: Oh, you again... What are you going to complain about?
TEXT.French: Oh, encore vous... De quoi êtes-vous venu vous plaindre ?
TEXT.German: Oh, you again... What are you going to complain about?
TEXT.Italian: Oh, you again... What are you going to complain about?
TEXT.Spanish: Oh, you again... What are you going to complain about?

TEXT.English: Treachery, cowardice and lies are everywhere - and your nation is no exception.
TEXT.French: La traîtrise, la lâcheté et les mensonges sont partout - et votre nation ne fait pas exception.
TEXT.German: Verrat, Feigheit und Lügen sind überall - und Eure Nation ist keine Ausnahme.
TEXT.Italian: Treachery, cowardice and lies are everywhere - and your nation is no exception.
TEXT.Spanish: Treachery, cowardice and lies are everywhere - and your nation is no exception.

TEXT.English: Speak fast [CT_CIV_ADJ]. I have enough on my schedule already.
TEXT.French: Parlez vite, [CT_CIV_ADJ]. Mon horaire est déjà assez rempli.
TEXT.German: Speak fast [CT_CIV_ADJ]. I have enough on my schedule already.
TEXT.Italian: Speak fast [CT_CIV_ADJ]. I have enough on my schedule already.
TEXT.Spanish: Speak fast [CT_CIV_ADJ]. I have enough on my schedule already.

TEXT.English: You lack the guile to trick me. Be warned I will not react well to deceit.
TEXT.French: Vous n'êtes pas assez rusé pour me duper. Soyez sûr que je réagirai très mal à toute trahison.
TEXT.German: Ihr seid nicht listig genug, um mich hereinzulegen. Ich warne Euch, ich reagiere nicht besonders erfreut auf Betrug.
TEXT.Italian: Non sei abbastanza furbo per fregarmi. Attento: non reagisco bene agli inganni.
TEXT.Spanish: Os falta astucia para engañarme. Os lo advierto: las triquiñuelas no son de mi agrado.

TEXT.English: The government of the [OUR_EMPIRE] will fulfill its duty to defend its independence and to repel foreign aggression, and accept the struggle to which it has been provoked!
TEXT.French: Le gouvernement du [OUR_EMPIRE] accomplira son devoir de défendre son indépendance et de repousser toute agression, et accepte de lutter en réponse à la provocation !
TEXT.German: The government of the [OUR_EMPIRE] will fulfill its duty to defend its independence, to repel foreign aggression, and accept the struggle to which it has been provoked!
TEXT.Italian: The government of the [OUR_EMPIRE] will fulfill its duty to defend its independence, to repel foreign aggression, and accept the struggle to which it has been provoked!
TEXT.Spanish: The government of the [OUR_EMPIRE] will fulfill its duty to defend its independence, to repel foreign aggression, and accept the struggle to which it has been provoked!

TEXT.English: No way! I shall punish you for your crimes against [OUR_CIV_SHORT] and its people!
TEXT.French: Jamais ! Je vous punirai pour vos crimes contre le [OUR_CIV_SHORT] et son peuple !
TEXT.German: No way! I shall punish you for your crimes against [OUR_CIV_SHORT] and its people!
TEXT.Italian: No way! I shall punish you for your crimes against [OUR_CIV_SHORT] and its people!
TEXT.Spanish: No way! I shall punish you for your crimes against [OUR_CIV_SHORT] and its people!

TEXT.English: I knew you would beg for peace eventually, but there will be no peace until you surrender.
TEXT.French: Je savais que vous finiriez par me supplier de faire la paix, mais il n'y aura aucune paix avant votre capitulation.
TEXT.German: Ich wusste, dass Ihr irgendwann um Frieden betteln würdet, aber es wird erst Frieden geben, wenn Ihr Euch ergebt.
TEXT.Italian: Sapevo che mi avresti pregato di stipulare una pace, alla fine, ma non ci sarà pace fino alla tua resa.
TEXT.Spanish: Sabía que, tarde o temprano, suplicaríais la paz. Pero no habrá paz hasta que os rindáis.

TEXT.English: Get out of my office!
TEXT.French: Sortez de mon bureau !
TEXT.German: Get out of my office!
TEXT.Italian: Get out of my office!
TEXT.Spanish: Get out of my office!

TEXT.English: You make me sad, [CT_NAME]. Go away.
TEXT.French: Vous m'attristez, [CT_NAME]. Partez.
TEXT.German: You make me sad, [CT_NAME]. Go away.
TEXT.Italian: You make me sad, [CT_NAME]. Go away.
TEXT.Spanish: You make me sad, [CT_NAME]. Go away.

TEXT.English: I will now use my cunning knowledge of tactics to ignore you.
TEXT.French: Je vais maintenant vous démontrer mes talents de stratège en vous ignorant totalement.
TEXT.German: Ich werde jetzt mein überragendes taktisches Wissen verwenden und Euch ignorieren.
TEXT.Italian: Ora userò la mia incredibile conoscenza della tattica per ignorarti.
TEXT.Spanish: Ahora utilizaré mi astuto conocimiento de la táctica para hacer caso omiso de vos.

TEXT.English: Your words are but the grunts of a diseased pig, [CT_NAME]. I do not hear them.
TEXT.French: Vos paroles sonnent à mes oreilles tels les horribles grognements d'un porc agonisant, [CT_NAME]. Je ne les écouterai pas plus longtemps.
TEXT.German: Ihr sprecht mit gespaltener Zunge, [CT_NAME], und ich will es nicht hören!
TEXT.Italian: Le tue parole risuonano come i grugniti di un maiale morente, [CT_NAME]. Un rumore fastidioso che non voglio udire.
TEXT.Spanish: Vuestras palabras no son más que gruñidos de un cerdo enfermo, [CT_NAME]. Como tales, no las escucho.

TEXT.English: Give me this, [CT_NAME] and perhaps our two nations can live in peace for a while longer.
TEXT.French: Donnez-moi ce que je demande, [CT_NAME], et peut-être nos deux nations pourront-elles cohabiter en paix quelque temps encore.
TEXT.German: Gebt uns, was wir verlangen, [CT_NAME], dann besteht die Chance, dass unsere Zivilisationen noch eine Weile in Frieden miteinander leben!
TEXT.Italian: Dammi questo, [CT_NAME], e forse le nostre due nazioni vivranno in pace per un altro po'.
TEXT.Spanish: Dadme esto, [CT_NAME], y es posible que nuestras naciones puedan vivir en paz un poco más.

TEXT.English: Hand this over, [CT_NAME], and I might let you continue to exist for a short while longer.
TEXT.French: Donnez-nous ce tribut, [CT_NAME], et il est possible que je vous laisse vivre... quelque temps, en tout cas.
TEXT.German: Her damit, [CT_NAME]! Dann werde ich Euch vielleicht noch eine Weile verschonen!
TEXT.Italian: Dammelo, [CT_NAME], e potrei lasciarti continuare a esistere ancora un po'.
TEXT.Spanish: Entregadnos esto, [CT_NAME] y puede que os deje perdurar un poco más.

TEXT.English: Unlikely as it may seem, it appears that your puny civilization has something that we want. I suggest you hand it over quickly.
TEXT.French: Aussi ahurissant que cela puisse paraître, il semblerait que votre ridicule petite civilisation dispose de quelque chose qui pourrait nous être utile. Je vous suggère de nous le délivrer au plus vite.
TEXT.German: So unglaublich es auch klingen mag: Eure mickrige Zivilisation scheint tatsächlich etwas zu haben, was wir wollen. Ihr wärt gut beraten, es uns schnellstens zu überlassen!
TEXT.Italian: Per quanto possa apparire improbabile, a quanto pare la tua insignificante civiltà possiede qualcosa che vogliamo. Ti consiglio di darcelo subito.
TEXT.Spanish: Por extraño que suene, parece que vuestra civilización tiene algo que queremos. Os sugiero que nos lo deis rápidamente.

TEXT.English: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. And how is that undefended civilization of yours coming along?
TEXT.French: Bienvenue, [CT_NAME]. Alors, comment évolue donc la situation dans votre petite civilisation si vulnérable ?
TEXT.German: Willkommen, [CT_NAME]! Und, wie stehen die Dinge in Eurer hilflosen kleinen Zivilisation?
TEXT.Italian: Salve, [CT_NAME]. Come vanno le cose per la tua civiltà indifesa?
TEXT.Spanish: Saludos, [CT_NAME]. ¿Cómo está esa civilización indefensa de la que venís?

TEXT.English: Not a chance. The mighty [OUR_CIV_ADJ] people do not care to make peace with cattle-stealing brigands like you.
TEXT.French: N'y comptez pas ! Le puissant peuple des [OUR_CIV_ADJ] ne souhaite pas faire la paix avec des vils voleurs de bétail de votre espèce.
TEXT.German: Keine Chance! Das mächtige [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3] Volk hat kein Interesse daran, mit miesen Viehdieben wie Euch Frieden zu schließen!
TEXT.Italian: Neanche per idea. Al potente sovrano [OUR_CIV_ADJ] non può interessare la pace con briganti ladri di bestiame come voi.
TEXT.Spanish: Ni en broma. El poderoso pueblo [OUR_CIV_ADJ:1] no se molesta ni en hacer las paces con cuatreros bergantes como vosotros.

TEXT.English: Greetings, [CT_NAME]! The [OUR_CIV_ADJ] people always enjoy meeting vulnerable and undefended new civilizations!
TEXT.French: Mes hommages, [CT_NAME] ! Le peuple des [OUR_CIV_ADJ] est toujours enchanté de rencontrer de nouvelles civilisations vulnérables et sans défense !
TEXT.German: Seid gegrüßt, [CT_NAME]! Das [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3] Volk ist stets hoch erfreut, die Bekanntschaft schutz- und wehrloser neuer Zivilisationen zu machen!
TEXT.Italian: Salve, [CT_NAME]! Il sovrano [OUR_CIV_ADJ] è sempre lieto di incontrare nuove civiltà vulnerabili e indifese!
TEXT.Spanish: ¡Saludos, [CT_NAME]! El pueblo [OUR_CIV_ADJ:1] siempre se congratula de encontrarse con civilizaciones vulnerables e indefensas.

TEXT.English: So you have emerged from your fetid country and come to me, [CT_NAME]. To what do I owe this extremely dubious honor?
TEXT.French: Vous avez enfin réussi à sortir de cet horrible pays pour venir me voir, [CT_NAME]. Que me vaut un pareil honneur ?
TEXT.German: Oha, Ihr habt Euer stinkendes Land verlassen, um mich zu besuchen, [CT_NAME]? Was verschafft mir denn diese zweifelhafte Ehre?
TEXT.Italian: E così hai lasciato quel tuo fetido paese e sei venuto da me, [CT_NAME]. E a cosa devo questo dubbio onore?
TEXT.Spanish: Así que habéis salido de vuestro fétido país y habéis venido a verme, [CT_NAME]. ¿A qué debo tan dudoso honor?

TEXT.English: A Mutual Protection Pact - Each Party Agrees to Automatically Declare War if the Other Party is Attacked.
TEXT.French: Pacte d'assistance mutuelle : chaque partie accepte de déclarer automatiquement la guerre si l'autre est attaquée.
TEXT.German: Ein Verteidigungsbündnis - Beide Parteien stimmen zu, den Angreifern der anderen Partei automatisch den Krieg zu erklären.
TEXT.Italian: Un patto di protezione reciproca: ogni civiltà accetta di dichiarare automaticamente guerra se la civiltà alleata viene attaccata.
TEXT.Spanish: Un acuerdo de protección mutua: cada parte accede a declarar automáticamente la guerra si alguien ataca a la otra.

TEXT.English: Slave Trade
TEXT.French: Commerce des esclaves
TEXT.German: Sklavenhandel
TEXT.Italian: Slave Trade
TEXT.Spanish: Slave Trade

TEXT.English: Regions
TEXT.French: Régions
TEXT.German: Regionen
TEXT.Italian: Regioni
TEXT.Spanish: Regiones

TEXT.English: Good day and bonjour to you, [CT_NAME]. The [OUR_CIV_ADJ] people wish for peace, but insists that masters in our own house we must be.
TEXT.French: Bonjour et good day, [CT_NAME]. Le peuple [OUR_CIV_ADJ] souhaite la paix, mais nous insistons pour être maîtres chez nous.
TEXT.German: Good day and bonjour, to you [CT_NAME]. The [OUR_CIV_ADJ] people wish for peace, but insist that masters in our own house we must be.
TEXT.Italian: Good day and bonjour, to you [CT_NAME]. The [OUR_CIV_ADJ] people wish for peace, but insist that masters in our own house we must be.
TEXT.Spanish: Good day and bonjour, to you [CT_NAME]. The [OUR_CIV_ADJ] people wish for peace, but insist that masters in our own house we must be.

TEXT.English: "You sacked one of our cities!"
TEXT.French: "Vous avez saccagé l'une de nos villes !"
TEXT.German: "Ihr habt eine unserer Städte geplündert!"
TEXT.Italian: "Hai saccheggiato una delle nostre città!"
TEXT.Spanish: "¡Saqueasteis una de nuestras ciudades!"

TEXT.English: Well? I have larger matters to attend to than the envoys of petty nations. Get on with it!
TEXT.French: Well? I have larger matters to attend to than the envoys of petty nations. Get on with it!
TEXT.German: Well? I have larger matters to attend to than the envoys of petty nations. Get on with it!
TEXT.Italian: Well? I have larger matters to attend to than the envoys of petty nations. Get on with it!
TEXT.Spanish: Well? I have larger matters to attend to than the envoys of petty nations. Get on with it!

TEXT.English: A man, a plan... A man, a plan, a waterway? No, no... A man, a pla- OH! I didn't see you there. Well met, [CT_NAME]! My name is [OUR_NAME], but you can call me Teddy.
TEXT.French: A man, a plan... A man, a plan, a waterway? No, no... A man, a pla- OH! I didn't see you there. Well met, [CT_NAME]! My name is [OUR_NAME], but you can call me Teddy.
TEXT.German: A man, a plan... A man, a plan, a waterway? No, no... A man, a pla- OH! I didn't see you there. Well met, [CT_NAME]! My name is [OUR_NAME], but you can call me Teddy.
TEXT.Italian: A man, a plan... A man, a plan, a waterway? No, no... A man, a pla- OH! I didn't see you there. Well met, [CT_NAME]! My name is [OUR_NAME], but you can call me Teddy.
TEXT.Spanish: A man, a plan... A man, a plan, a waterway? No, no... A man, a pla- OH! I didn't see you there. Well met, [CT_NAME]! My name is [OUR_NAME], but you can call me Teddy.

TEXT.English: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. I AM a jelly donut.
TEXT.French: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. I AM a jelly donut.
TEXT.German: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. I AM a jelly donut.
TEXT.Italian: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. I AM a jelly donut.
TEXT.Spanish: Greetings, [CT_NAME]. I AM a jelly donut.

TEXT.English: Howdy y'all, name's [OUR_NAME]. How would you like to witness a full nuclear arsenal of 400 LGM-30G Minuteman III Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles barrelling down on your sorry nation? I thought not.
TEXT.French: Howdy y'all, name's [OUR_NAME]. How would you like to witness a full nuclear arsenal of 400 LGM-30G Minuteman III Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles barrelling down on your sorry nation? I thought not.
TEXT.German: Howdy y'all, name's [OUR_NAME]. How would you like to witness a full nuclear arsenal of 400 LGM-30G Minuteman III Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles barrelling down on your sorry nation? I thought not.

TEXT.English: Why can't I just eat my waffle? [ICON_HAPPY] xoxo
TEXT.French: Why can't I just eat my waffle? [ICON_HAPPY] xoxo
TEXT.German: Why can't I just eat my waffle? [ICON_HAPPY] xoxo
TEXT.Italian: Why can't I just eat my waffle? [ICON_HAPPY] xoxo
TEXT.Spanish: Why can't I just eat my waffle? [ICON_HAPPY] xoxo

TEXT.English: My homeland is an enigma to my people, but yours shall not be - cause I'm going to invade it.
TEXT.French: My homeland is an enigma to my people, but yours shall not be - cause I'm going to invade it.
TEXT.German: My homeland is an enigma to my people, but yours shall not be - cause I'm going to invade it.
TEXT.Italian: My homeland is an enigma to my people, but yours shall not be - cause I'm going to invade it.
TEXT.Spanish: My homeland is an enigma to my people, but yours shall not be - cause I'm going to invade it.

TEXT.English: They say the caliber of a leader depends on what he is made of. My people came from the clouds, the very heavens above. What are you made of?
TEXT.French: They say the caliber of a leader depends on what he is made of. My people came from the clouds, the very heavens above. What are you made of?
TEXT.German: They say the caliber of a leader depends on what he is made of. My people came from the clouds, the very heavens above. What are you made of?
TEXT.Italian: They say the caliber of a leader depends on what he is made of. My people came from the clouds, the very heavens above. What are you made of?
TEXT.Spanish: They say the caliber of a leader depends on what he is made of. My people came from the clouds, the very heavens above. What are you made of?

TEXT.English: I am [OUR_NAME] of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. You may enter our lands as a guest, [CT_NAME]. Do not mistake that for permission to become our master.
TEXT.French: I am [OUR_NAME] of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. You may enter our lands as a guest, [CT_NAME]. Do not mistake that for permission to become our master.
TEXT.German: I am [OUR_NAME] of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. You may enter our lands as a guest, [CT_NAME]. Do not mistake that for permission to become our master.
TEXT.Italian: I am [OUR_NAME] of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. You may enter our lands as a guest, [CT_NAME]. Do not mistake that for permission to become our master.
TEXT.Spanish: I am [OUR_NAME] of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. You may enter our lands as a guest, [CT_NAME]. Do not mistake that for permission to become our master.

TEXT.English: They call me the Earthshaker. Pray my armies don't crumble your walls with their approach.
TEXT.French: They call me the Earthshaker. Pray my armies don't crumble your walls with their approach.
TEXT.German: They call me the Earthshaker. Pray my armies don't crumble your walls with their approach.
TEXT.Italian: They call me the Earthshaker. Pray my armies don't crumble your walls with their approach.
TEXT.Spanish: They call me the Earthshaker. Pray my armies don't crumble your walls with their approach.

TEXT.English: Aloha, [CT_NAME]. I am [OUR_NAME]. There is room in my harbors for your ships, if you come to trade.
TEXT.French: Aloha, [CT_NAME]. I am [OUR_NAME]. There is room in my harbors for your ships, if you come to trade.
TEXT.German: Aloha, [CT_NAME]. I am [OUR_NAME]. There is room in my harbors for your ships, if you come to trade.
TEXT.Italian: Aloha, [CT_NAME]. I am [OUR_NAME]. There is room in my harbors for your ships, if you come to trade.
TEXT.Spanish: Aloha, [CT_NAME]. I am [OUR_NAME]. There is room in my harbors for your ships, if you come to trade.

TEXT.English: I am [OUR_NAME], chief of the [OUR_CIV_ADJ] people. Let us trade and strengthen our friendship.
TEXT.French: Je suis [OUR_NAME], chef des [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3]. Commençons par commercer pour renforcer notre amitié
TEXT.German: Ich bin [OUR_NAME], Oberhaupt des [OUR_CIV_ADJ:2] Volkes. Lasst uns Handel treiben und unsere Freundschaft stärken.
TEXT.Italian: Sono [OUR_NAME], capo del popolo [OUR_CIV_ADJ]. Commerciamo e consolidiamo la nostra amicizia.
TEXT.Spanish: Soy [OUR_NAME], jefe del pueblo [OUR_CIV_ADJ:1]. Comerciemos y estrechemos nuestros lazos de amistad.

TEXT.English: Welcome. I am [OUR_NAME] of the [OUR_CIV_ADJ]. I pray that you and your people value peace as much as we do.
TEXT.French: Bienvenue. Je suis [OUR_NAME] des [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3]. Je prie pour que la paix ait autant de valeur à vos yeux qu'aux nôtres.
TEXT.German: Willkommen. Ich bin [OUR_NAME] vom [OUR_CIV_ADJ:2] Volk. Ich bete darum, dass Ihr und Euer Volk den Frieden ebenso sehr schätzt wie wir.
TEXT.Italian: Benvenuto. Sono [OUR_NAME] della civiltà [OUR_CIV_ADJ]. Prego che tu e il tuo popolo diate tanto valore alla pace quanto gliene diamo noi.
TEXT.Spanish: Bienvenido. Soy [OUR_NAME], de los [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3]. Rezo porque vuestro pueblo valore la paz tanto como nosotros.

TEXT.English: Hello, traveler from the Great Sea. I am Cacique [OUR_NAME] of the [OUR_CIV_ADJ] tribe. Let us share this land and grow as friends.
TEXT.French: Bonjour, voyageur des mers. Je suis le cacique [OUR_NAME] de la tribu des [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3]. Partageons-nous ces terres et devenons amis !
TEXT.German: Hallo, Reisender vom Großen Meer. Ich bin Kazike [OUR_NAME] vom [OUR_CIV_ADJ:2] Stamm. Lasst uns dieses Land teilen und als Freunde darin leben.
TEXT.Italian: Salve, viaggiatore che arriva dal grande mare. Sono il cacique [OUR_NAME] della tribù [OUR_CIV_ADJ]. Dividiamoci questa terra e diventiamo amici.
TEXT.Spanish: Hola, viajero del Gran Mar. Soy el cacique [OUR_NAME] de la tribu [OUR_CIV_ADJ:2]. Compartamos esta tierra y seamos amigos.

TEXT.English: Hello, pale one. I, [OUR_NAME] of the [OUR_CIV_ADJ] people, welcome you. Let us feast in your honor.
TEXT.French: Bonjour, visage pâle. Moi, [OUR_NAME], chef des [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3] vous souhaite la bienvenue. Allons festoyer en votre honneur.
TEXT.German: Hallo, Bleichgesicht. Ich, [OUR_NAME] vom [OUR_CIV_ADJ:2] Volk, heiße Euch willkommen. Lasst uns zu Euren Ehren ein Fest veranstalten.
TEXT.Italian: Saluti, viso pallido. Io, [OUR_NAME] del popolo [OUR_CIV_ADJ], ti do il benvenuto. Facciamo festa in tuo onore.
TEXT.Spanish: Hola, rostro pálido. Yo, [OUR_NAME] del pueblo [OUR_CIV_ADJ:1] os doy la bienvenida. Daremos un festín en vuestro honor.

TEXT.English: I am Toussaint Louverture. [OUR_CIV_SHORT] welcomes commerce and friendship, [CT_NAME], but our people are no longer for sale.
TEXT.French: I am Toussaint Louverture. [OUR_CIV_SHORT] welcomes commerce and friendship, [CT_NAME], but our people are no longer for sale.
TEXT.German: I am Toussaint Louverture. [OUR_CIV_SHORT] welcomes commerce and friendship, [CT_NAME], but our people are no longer for sale.
TEXT.Italian: I am Toussaint Louverture. [OUR_CIV_SHORT] welcomes commerce and friendship, [CT_NAME], but our people are no longer for sale.
TEXT.Spanish: I am Toussaint Louverture. [OUR_CIV_SHORT] welcomes commerce and friendship, [CT_NAME], but our people are no longer for sale.

TEXT.English: I am pleased to meet you, [CT_NAME]! I offer you a treaty of peace, I suggest you accept it.
TEXT.French: C'est un plaisir de faire votre connaissance, [CT_NAME] ! Je vous propose un traité de paix et je vous suggère de l'accepter.
TEXT.German: Ich freue mich, Euch kennenzulernen, [CT_NAME]! Ich biete Euch einen Friedensvertrag an, den Ihr annehmen solltet.
TEXT.Italian: Sono contento di incontrarti, [CT_NAME]! Ti offro un trattato di pace... e ti suggerisco di accettarlo.
TEXT.Spanish: Me alegro mucho de conoceros, [CT_NAME]. Os ofrezco un tratado de paz. Os sugiero que lo aceptéis.

TEXT.English: I am Jefferson Davis, President of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. We intend to manage our own affairs, [CT_NAME]. I trust you will manage yours.
TEXT.French: I am Jefferson Davis, President of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. We intend to manage our own affairs, [CT_NAME]. I trust you will manage yours.
TEXT.German: I am Jefferson Davis, President of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. We intend to manage our own affairs, [CT_NAME]. I trust you will manage yours.
TEXT.Italian: I am Jefferson Davis, President of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. We intend to manage our own affairs, [CT_NAME]. I trust you will manage yours.
TEXT.Spanish: I am Jefferson Davis, President of [OUR_CIV_SHORT]. We intend to manage our own affairs, [CT_NAME]. I trust you will manage yours.

TEXT.English: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Sit down. There is more profit in trading coffee than in trading cannon fire.
TEXT.French: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Sit down. There is more profit in trading coffee than in trading cannon fire.
TEXT.German: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Sit down. There is more profit in trading coffee than in trading cannon fire.
TEXT.Italian: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Sit down. There is more profit in trading coffee than in trading cannon fire.
TEXT.Spanish: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Sit down. There is more profit in trading coffee than in trading cannon fire.

TEXT.English: You change your promises more often than I have changed uniforms, [CT_NAME]. What is it this time?
TEXT.French: You change your promises more often than I have changed uniforms, [CT_NAME]. What is it this time?
TEXT.German: You change your promises more often than I have changed uniforms, [CT_NAME]. What is it this time?
TEXT.Italian: You change your promises more often than I have changed uniforms, [CT_NAME]. What is it this time?
TEXT.Spanish: You change your promises more often than I have changed uniforms, [CT_NAME]. What is it this time?

TEXT.English: It is good to talk to a person that understands the importance of action. Let us discuss how we can strengthen our nations.
TEXT.French: C'est bon de parler à quelqu'un qui comprend l'importance de l'action. Voyons comment nous pourrions renforcer nos nations.
TEXT.German: Es ist gut, sich mit jemandem zu unterhalten, der weiß, wie wichtig es ist zu handeln. Lasst uns darüber diskutieren, wie wir unsere Nationen stärken können.
TEXT.Italian: È bello parlare con una persona che capisce l'importanza dell'azione. Parliamo di come possiamo rafforzare le nostre nazioni.
TEXT.Spanish: Es bueno hablar con alguien que entiende la importancia de los actos. Charlemos sobre cómo podemos fortalecer nuestras naciones.

TEXT.English: Go on, say what you want. Let us see if it will quell my contempt for you.
TEXT.French: Allez-y, dites ce que vous avez à dire. Voyons si ça apaisera mon mépris envers vous.
TEXT.German: Sagt, was Ihr zu sagen habt. Vielleicht ändert ja irgendetwas davon meine verächtliche Meinung über Euch.
TEXT.Italian: Coraggio, dimmi quello che vuoi. Vediamo se soffocherà il disprezzo che provo per te.
TEXT.Spanish: Adelante, decidme lo que queréis. Veremos si eso acaba con el desdén que siento hacia vos.

TEXT.English: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Our ports could use more merchants and fewer gunboats. What business brings you here?
TEXT.French: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Our ports could use more merchants and fewer gunboats. What business brings you here?
TEXT.German: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Our ports could use more merchants and fewer gunboats. What business brings you here?
TEXT.Italian: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Our ports could use more merchants and fewer gunboats. What business brings you here?
TEXT.Spanish: Welcome, [CT_NAME]. Our ports could use more merchants and fewer gunboats. What business brings you here?

TEXT.English: You are not addressing one of your provincial governors, [CT_NAME]. State your business.
TEXT.French: You are not addressing one of your provincial governors, [CT_NAME]. State your business.
TEXT.German: You are not addressing one of your provincial governors, [CT_NAME]. State your business.
TEXT.Italian: You are not addressing one of your provincial governors, [CT_NAME]. State your business.
TEXT.Spanish: You are not addressing one of your provincial governors, [CT_NAME]. State your business.

TEXT.English: You may keep your promises, [CT_NAME]. I have soldiers to attend to.
TEXT.French: You may keep your promises, [CT_NAME]. I have soldiers to attend to.
TEXT.German: You may keep your promises, [CT_NAME]. I have soldiers to attend to.
TEXT.Italian: You may keep your promises, [CT_NAME]. I have soldiers to attend to.
TEXT.Spanish: You may keep your promises, [CT_NAME]. I have soldiers to attend to.

TEXT.English: Look, I'm very busy. Why don't you take the kids and go back to the clubhouse?
TEXT.French: Ecoutez, je suis très occupé. Pourquoi n'iriez-vous pas faire quelques pâtés de sable ?
TEXT.German: Seht, ich bin sehr beschäftigt. Warum nehmt Ihr nicht die Kinder und geht zum Clubhaus zurück?
TEXT.Italian: Senti, sono molto occupato. Perché non prendi i bambini e te ne torni al circolo?
TEXT.Spanish: Mirad, estoy muy ocupado. ¿Por qué no os lleváis a los niños y os volvéis al club?

TEXT.English: My cabinet has more pressing business than hearing your objections, [CT_NAME].
TEXT.French: My cabinet has more pressing business than hearing your objections, [CT_NAME].
TEXT.German: My cabinet has more pressing business than hearing your objections, [CT_NAME].
TEXT.Italian: My cabinet has more pressing business than hearing your objections, [CT_NAME].
TEXT.Spanish: My cabinet has more pressing business than hearing your objections, [CT_NAME].

TEXT.English: No peace yet. My soldiers did not break their chains merely to surrender their arms.
TEXT.French: No peace yet. My soldiers did not break their chains merely to surrender their arms.
TEXT.German: No peace yet. My soldiers did not break their chains merely to surrender their arms.
TEXT.Italian: No peace yet. My soldiers did not break their chains merely to surrender their arms.
TEXT.Spanish: No peace yet. My soldiers did not break their chains merely to surrender their arms.

TEXT.English: Peace? There will be peace when you surrender!
TEXT.French: La paix ? Il ne pourra y avoir de paix que lorsque vous vous serez rendu !
TEXT.German: Frieden? Es gibt erst Frieden, wenn Ihr Euch ergebt!
TEXT.Italian: Pace? Ci sarà la pace quando ti arrenderai!
TEXT.Spanish: ¿Paz? ¡La tendremos cuando os rindáis!

TEXT.English: We shall not sign away at the negotiating table what our armies still hold in the field.
TEXT.French: We shall not sign away at the negotiating table what our armies still hold in the field.
TEXT.German: We shall not sign away at the negotiating table what our armies still hold in the field.
TEXT.Italian: We shall not sign away at the negotiating table what our armies still hold in the field.
TEXT.Spanish: We shall not sign away at the negotiating table what our armies still hold in the field.

TEXT.English: Our treasury is thin, [CT_NAME], but our memory is long. A contribution would not be forgotten.
TEXT.French: Our treasury is thin, [CT_NAME], but our memory is long. A contribution would not be forgotten.
TEXT.German: Our treasury is thin, [CT_NAME], but our memory is long. A contribution would not be forgotten.
TEXT.Italian: Our treasury is thin, [CT_NAME], but our memory is long. A contribution would not be forgotten.
TEXT.Spanish: Our treasury is thin, [CT_NAME], but our memory is long. A contribution would not be forgotten.

TEXT.English: An army cannot march on declarations of liberty. Send these supplies, and spare us both an unpleasant discussion.
TEXT.French: An army cannot march on declarations of liberty. Send these supplies, and spare us both an unpleasant discussion.
TEXT.German: An army cannot march on declarations of liberty. Send these supplies, and spare us both an unpleasant discussion.
TEXT.Italian: An army cannot march on declarations of liberty. Send these supplies, and spare us both an unpleasant discussion.
TEXT.Spanish: An army cannot march on declarations of liberty. Send these supplies, and spare us both an unpleasant discussion.

TEXT.English: My soldiers have driven off greater armies than yours, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand before they must prove it again.
TEXT.French: My soldiers have driven off greater armies than yours, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand before they must prove it again.
TEXT.German: My soldiers have driven off greater armies than yours, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand before they must prove it again.
TEXT.Italian: My soldiers have driven off greater armies than yours, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand before they must prove it again.
TEXT.Spanish: My soldiers have driven off greater armies than yours, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand before they must prove it again.

TEXT.English: The [OUR_EMPIRE] are in dire need, please help us.
TEXT.French: L'[OUR_EMPIRE] est en grand désarroi. Je vous en prie, aidez-nous.
TEXT.German: Das [OUR_EMPIRE:2] leidet große Not, bitte helft uns.
TEXT.Italian: Abbiamo urgente bisogno, per favore aiutaci.
TEXT.Spanish: El [OUR_EMPIRE] tiene una terrible necesidad. Ayudadnos, por favor.

TEXT.English: My people need what you have. How about you give it to them and show that you are interested in peaceful resolutions to problems.
TEXT.French: Mon peuple a besoin de ce que vous avez. Accédez à nos demandes et vous prouverez votre volonté à trouver une solution pacifique aux problèmes.
TEXT.German: Mein Volk braucht, was Ihr habt. Wie wäre es, wenn Ihr es ihm gebt und so zeigt, dass Ihr an einer friedlichen Lösung von Problemen interessiert seid?
TEXT.Italian: La mia gente ha bisogno di quello che hai. Che ne dici di darglielo e mostrare così di essere interessato a una soluzione pacifica dei problemi?
TEXT.Spanish: Mi pueblo necesita lo que tenéis. ¿Qué tal si se lo dais y demostráis así vuestro interés en resolver pacíficamente los problemas?

TEXT.English: You are not in a position to negotiate. Give my people what they want.
TEXT.French: Vous n'êtes pas en position de négocier. Donnez à mon peuple ce qu'il veut.
TEXT.German: Es steht Euch nicht zu, zu verhandeln. Gebt meinem Volk, was es will.
TEXT.Italian: Non sei nelle condizioni di negoziare. Dai al mio popolo ciò che chiede.
TEXT.Spanish: No estáis en posición de negociar. Dadle a mi pueblo lo que quiere.

TEXT.English: Our cotton ought to secure us friends abroad, [CT_NAME]. This assistance would demonstrate that you are one of them.
TEXT.French: Our cotton ought to secure us friends abroad, [CT_NAME]. This assistance would demonstrate that you are one of them.
TEXT.German: Our cotton ought to secure us friends abroad, [CT_NAME]. This assistance would demonstrate that you are one of them.
TEXT.Italian: Our cotton ought to secure us friends abroad, [CT_NAME]. This assistance would demonstrate that you are one of them.
TEXT.Spanish: Our cotton ought to secure us friends abroad, [CT_NAME]. This assistance would demonstrate that you are one of them.

TEXT.English: Let us spare our treasuries the expense of a campaign, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand.
TEXT.French: Let us spare our treasuries the expense of a campaign, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand.
TEXT.German: Let us spare our treasuries the expense of a campaign, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand.
TEXT.Italian: Let us spare our treasuries the expense of a campaign, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand.
TEXT.Spanish: Let us spare our treasuries the expense of a campaign, [CT_NAME]. Meet this demand.

TEXT.English: Our armies are ready, [CT_NAME]. I suggest you settle this account before they collect it.
TEXT.French: Our armies are ready, [CT_NAME]. I suggest you settle this account before they collect it.
TEXT.German: Our armies are ready, [CT_NAME]. I suggest you settle this account before they collect it.
TEXT.Italian: Our armies are ready, [CT_NAME]. I suggest you settle this account before they collect it.
TEXT.Spanish: Our armies are ready, [CT_NAME]. I suggest you settle this account before they collect it.

TEXT.English: At this time words can resolve nothing.
TEXT.French: A ce stade, parler ne résoudra rien.
TEXT.German: Zu diesem Zeitpunkt können Worte nichts bewirken.
TEXT.Italian: A questo punto le parole non possono risolvere nulla.
TEXT.Spanish: A estas alturas, las palabras no pueden resolver nada.

TEXT.English: After the atrocities you have committed there can be no peace!
TEXT.French: Après les atrocités que vous avez commises, il n'y aura jamais de paix !
TEXT.German: Nach den unzähligen Gräueltaten, die Ihr verbrochen habt, kann es keinen Frieden geben!
TEXT.Italian: Dopo le atrocità che hai commesso non può esserci alcuna pace!
TEXT.Spanish: Después de las atrocidades que habéis cometido, no puede haber paz.

TEXT.English: It is always good to hear from friends. Let us sit and talk.
TEXT.French: C'est toujours un plaisir de revoir ses amis ! Asseyons-nous et discutons.
TEXT.German: Es ist immer schön, wenn sich Freunde bei einem melden. Lasst uns in Ruhe reden.
TEXT.Italian: È sempre bello avere notizie degli amici. Sediamoci e parliamo.
TEXT.Spanish: Siempre es un placer oír al [CT_EMPIRE]. Sentémonos y hablemos.

TEXT.English: I hope you have come to try to atone for your actions.
TEXT.French: J'espère que vous êtes venu expier vos péchés.
TEXT.German: Ich hoffe, Ihr seid hier, um Abbitte für Eure Taten zu leisten.
TEXT.Italian: Spero che tu sia qui per cercare di espiare le tue azioni.
TEXT.Spanish: Espero que hayáis venido a intentar enmendar vuestros actos.

TEXT.English: The spirits have told me of your generosity. I hope they are not wrong.
TEXT.French: Les esprits m'ont parlé de votre générosité. J'espère qu'ils n'ont pas tort.
TEXT.German: Die Geister haben mir von Eurer Großzügigkeit erzählt. Ich hoffe, dass sie sich nicht geirrt haben.
TEXT.Italian: Gli spiriti mi hanno parlato della tua generosità. Spero che non si sbagliassero.
TEXT.Spanish: Los espíritus me han hablado de vuestra generosidad. Espero que no se hayan equivocado.

TEXT.English: We have given you much and asked for nothing in return...until now.
TEXT.French: Nous vous avons beaucoup donné sans rien demander en échange... jusqu'à maintenant.
TEXT.German: Wir haben Euch viel gegeben und im Austausch um nichts gebeten ... bis jetzt.
TEXT.Italian: Ti abbiamo dato tanto, senza volere nulla in cambio... fino a ora.
TEXT.Spanish: Hasta ahora os hemos dado mucho y no os hemos pedido nada a cambio.

TEXT.English: It is dangerous for the rabbit to tempt the wolf. Give us what we want.
TEXT.French: C'est dangereux pour un lapin de tenter le loup. Donnez-nous ce que nous voulons.
TEXT.German: Es ist für das Kaninchen gefährlich, den Wolf zu reizen. Gebt uns, was wir wollen.
TEXT.Italian: È pericoloso, per il coniglio, provocare il lupo. Dacci quello che vogliamo.
TEXT.Spanish: Es peligroso para el conejo provocar al lobo. Dadnos lo que queremos.

TEXT.English: Greetings, I am [OUR_NAME] of the [OUR_CIV_ADJ]. Let us sit by the fire and talk.
TEXT.French: Bonjour, je suis [OUR_NAME] des [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3]. Allons discuter autour du feu.
TEXT.German: Seid gegrüßt, ich bin [OUR_NAME] vom [OUR_CIV_ADJ:2] Volk. Setzt Euch mit mir ans Feuer, damit wir reden können.
TEXT.Italian: Saluti, sono [OUR_NAME] della civiltà [OUR_CIV_ADJ]. Sediamoci davanti al fuoco e parliamo.
TEXT.Spanish: Saludos. Soy [OUR_NAME], de los [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3]. Sentémonos alrededor de la hoguera y hablemos.

TEXT.English: Perhaps you should go back to where you came from, I do not want to talk to you.
TEXT.French: Vous devriez peut-être retourner d'où vous venez. Je n'ai pas envie de vous parler.
TEXT.German: Vielleicht solltet Ihr dorthin zurückkehren, wo Ihr hergekommen seid. Ich will nicht mit Euch reden.
TEXT.Italian: Forse dovresti tornartene da dove vieni, non ho intenzione di parlarti.
TEXT.Spanish: Quizá deberíais volver por donde habéis venido. No quiero hablar con vos.

TEXT.English: I have no time to talk to you. I need to go eat.
TEXT.French: Je n'ai pas de temps à vous accorder. Je dois aller manger.
TEXT.German: Ich habe keine Zeit, mit Euch zu reden. Ich muss etwas essen.
TEXT.Italian: Non ho tempo di parlarti. Devo andare a mangiare.
TEXT.Spanish: No tengo tiempo para hablar con vos. Tengo que ir a comer.

TEXT.English: You are untrustworthy and do not deserve my attention.
TEXT.French: Vous n'êtes pas digne de confiance et ne méritez pas mon intérêt.
TEXT.German: Ihr seid unzuverlässig und verdient es nicht, beachtet zu werden.
TEXT.Italian: Non meriti fiducia e nemmeno la mia attenzione.
TEXT.Spanish: No sois de fiar y no os merecéis mi atención.

TEXT.English: I can't lose, so there is no reason for peace.
TEXT.French: Je ne peux pas perdre, alors je n'ai aucune raison de faire la paix.
TEXT.German: Ich kann unmöglich verlieren, also gibt es keinen Grund, Frieden zu schließen.
TEXT.Italian: Non posso perdere, quindi non c'è ragione di firmare una pace.
TEXT.Spanish: No puedo perder, así que no hay motivo para firmar la paz.

TEXT.English: You want us to make peace with you? The very idea makes me lose my appetite.
TEXT.French: Vous voulez faire la paix avec nous ? J'en perds l'appétit rien que d'y songer.
TEXT.German: Ihr wollt, dass wir mit Euch Frieden schließen? Der bloße Gedanke daran verdirbt mir bereits den Appetit.
TEXT.Italian: Vuoi che facciamo pace? La sola idea mi fa passare la fame.
TEXT.Spanish: ¿Y ahora queréis que hagamos las paces? Con solo pensar en ello se me revuelven las tripas.

TEXT.English: There will be no peace!
TEXT.French: Il n'y aura jamais de paix !
TEXT.German: Es wird keinen Frieden geben!
TEXT.Italian: Non ci sarà pace!
TEXT.Spanish: No habrá paz.

TEXT.English: Ah, my great friend has come to see me on this wonderful day. How can the [OUR_CIV_ADJ] be of service.
TEXT.French: Ah ! Quelle joie de voir mon bon ami, en ce jour merveilleux !
TEXT.German: Ah, ich bekomme Besuch an diesem wundervollen Tag. Wie kann Euch das [OUR_CIV_ADJ:3] Volk dienlich sein?
TEXT.Italian: Ah, il mio grande amico è venuto a trovarmi in questo meraviglioso giorno. Come esserti d'aiuto il popolo [OUR_CIV_ADJ]?
TEXT.Spanish: Ah, mi gran amigo ha venido a verme en este maravilloso día. ¿En qué puede ayudaros el [OUR_CIV_ADJ]?

TEXT.English: Welcome, my friend. Let us feast in your honor.
TEXT.French: Bienvenue, mon ami. Festoyons en votre honneur.
TEXT.German: Willkommen, mein Freund. Lasst uns zu Euren Ehren feiern.
TEXT.Italian: Benvenuto, amico mio. Festeggiamo in tuo onore.
TEXT.Spanish: Bienvenido, amigo. Celebremos un banquete en tu honor.

TEXT.English: Welcome, friend! Let us talk and trade.
TEXT.French: Bienvenue, mon ami ! Parlons un peu affaires !
TEXT.German: Willkommen! Lasst uns reden und Handel treiben.
TEXT.Italian: Benvenuto, amico! Parliamo e commerciamo.
TEXT.Spanish: Bienvenido, amigo. Hablemos y negociemos.

TEXT.English: If it is not the worst thing to ever wash in from the Great Sea. What do you want?
TEXT.French: Si ce n'est pas la pire saleté que la mer ait jamais rejetée ! Que voulez-vous ?
TEXT.German: Na wenn das nicht das Schlimmste ist, was das Große Meer jemals angespült hat. Was wollt Ihr?
TEXT.Italian: Guarda un po' se non è il peggior rifiuto che ci abbia consegnato la marea. Cosa vuoi?
TEXT.Spanish: Vaya, si es la peor cosa que ha traído el Gran Mar. ¿Qué queréis?

TEXT.English: Whatever it is you want, make it quick. My lunch is getting cold.
TEXT.French: Quoique vous vouliez, faites vite ! Mon dîner refroidit.
TEXT.German: Was Ihr auch wollt, macht schnell. Mein Essen wird kalt.
TEXT.Italian: Qualsiasi cosa tu voglia, sbrigati. Il pranzo si raffredda.
TEXT.Spanish: Sea lo que sea, sed breve. Se me está enfriando el almuerzo.

TEXT.English: You do not deserve my attention. Consider yourself lucky.
TEXT.French: Vous ne méritez pas mon attention. Et tant mieux pour vous.
TEXT.German: Ihr verdient meine Aufmerksamkeit nicht. Schätzt Euch glücklich.
TEXT.Italian: Non meriti la mia attenzione. Considerati fortunato.
TEXT.Spanish: No os merecéis mi atención. Consideraos afortunado.

TEXT.English: The greatest service friends can give to each other is charity. Please help us.
TEXT.French: Le plus grand service que des amis puissent se rendre, c'est la charité. Aidez-nous.
TEXT.German: Der größte Dienst, den ein Freund einem anderen erweisen kann, ist Wohltätigkeit. Bitte helft uns.
TEXT.Italian: Il più grande dono che si possono fare degli amici è la carità. Aiutaci, per favore.
TEXT.Spanish: El mayor servicio que pueden prestarse los amigos es la caridad. Ayudadnos, por favor.

TEXT.English: We are in need, but we have nothing to offer except the food on our tables. Please give us what we want and I'll be sure to invite you to our next soiree.
TEXT.French: Nous sommes dans le besoin, mais nous n'avons rien à vous offrir à part la nourriture qui garnit nos tables. Donnez-nous ce que nous voulons et nous vous inviterons à notre prochaine soirée.
TEXT.German: Wir sind in Not, aber wir können Euch nichts anderes anbieten als das Essen auf unserem Tisch. Gebt uns bitte, was wir benötigen, dann lade ich Euch auch bestimmt zu unserer nächsten Soiree ein.
TEXT.Italian: Abbiamo bisogno di aiuto ma non abbiamo altro da offrirti se non il cibo sulle nostre tavole. Dacci quello che vogliamo e ti inviteremo al prossimo ricevimento.
TEXT.Spanish: Estamos necesitados, pero no podemos ofreceros más que comida en nuestra mesa. Dadnos lo que precisamos, por favor, y me aseguraré de invitaros a nuestra próxima velada.

TEXT.English: Give me what I want and the spirits will watch over you.
TEXT.French: Donnez-moi ce que je veux et tous les esprits seront à vos côtés.
TEXT.German: Gebt mir, was ich verlange, dann werden die Geister über Euch wachen.
TEXT.Italian: Dammi quello che voglio e gli spiriti veglieranno su di te.
TEXT.Spanish: Dadnos lo que queremos y los espíritus velarán por vosotros.

TEXT.English: The difference between peace and war is often the answer to simple questions. Such as, will you help us?
TEXT.French: La différence entre la guerre et la paix se trouve souvent dans la réponse à de simples questions. Comme par exemple: "voulez-vous nous aider?"
TEXT.German: Oft entscheidet die Antwort auf eine einfache Frage zwischen Frieden und Krieg. Wie zum Beispiel: Werdet Ihr uns helfen?
TEXT.Italian: La differenza tra guerra e pace è spesso la risposta a semplici domande. Come, per esempio: ci aiuterai?
TEXT.Spanish: La diferencia entre la paz y la guerra suele estar en cómo se responde a las preguntas sencillas, preguntas como: "¿Nos ayudaréis?"

TEXT.English: My tribe needs assistance. If you want to be invited to dinner, then please help.
TEXT.French: Ma tribu a besoin d'aide. Si vous voulez être invité à dîner, alors aidez-nous.
TEXT.German: Mein Stamm braucht Hilfe. Wenn Ihr zum Essen eingeladen werden möchtet, helft uns bitte.
TEXT.Italian: La mia tribù ha bisogno di aiuto. Se vuoi essere invitato a cena, dacci una mano.
TEXT.Spanish: Mi tribu necesita ayuda. Si queréis que os invite a comer, ayudadnos, por favor.

TEXT.English: Please prove your friendship by giving us what we want.
TEXT.French: Renforcez votre amitié envers nous en nous donnant ce que nous voulons.
TEXT.German: Stellt Eure Freundschaft bitte unter Beweis und gebt uns, was wir verlangen.
TEXT.Italian: Provaci la tua amicizia dandoci quello che vogliamo.
TEXT.Spanish: Por favor, haced honor a nuestra amistad dándonos lo que queremos.

TEXT.English: If I was you, I would want to stay on my good side. Give my tribe what it requires.
TEXT.French: Si j'étais vous, je préfèrerais rester dans mes petits papiers. Donnez à ma tribu ce qu'elle réclame.
TEXT.German: Wenn ich an Eurer Stelle wäre, würde ich versuchen, mich weiterhin milde zu stimmen. Gebt meinem Stamm das, was er braucht.
TEXT.Italian: Se fossi in te, non tirerei troppo la corda. Dai alla mia tribù quanto chiede.
TEXT.Spanish: Yo de vos, intentaría estar a buenas conmigo. Dadle a mi tribu lo que pide.

TEXT.English: Give us what we want or you will learn the difference between being invited to dinner and being dinner.
TEXT.French: Donnez-nous ce que nous voulons ou vous apprendrez la différence entre être invité à dîner et être le dîner.
TEXT.German: Gebt uns was wir wollen, sonst lernt Ihr den Unterschied zwischen Essen HABEN und Essen SEIN kennen.
TEXT.Italian: Dacci quello che vogliamo o conoscerai la differenza tra l'essere invitato a cena e l'essere la cena.
TEXT.Spanish: Dadnos lo que queremos o sabréis la diferencia entre ser invitado a comer o ser la comida.

TEXT.English: It is our custom that you give us what we want, and in return we do not destroy you.
TEXT.French: La tradition exige que vous nous donniez ce que nous voulons. En échange, nous vous laisserons la vie sauve.
TEXT.German: Es ist bei uns Brauch, dass Ihr uns gebt, was wir verlangen, und wir Euch im Gegenzug nicht zerstören.
TEXT.Italian: È nostra usanza che tu ci dia quello che vogliamo, e in cambio noi non ti distruggeremo.
TEXT.Spanish: Es nuestra costumbre que nos deis lo que queremos y, a cambio, nosotros no acabamos con vosotros.

TEXT.Spanish: Let us settle this before our warriors must do it for us. Provide what I ask.
